title: Places worth twice
subtitle: Binary is decimal's idea with two digits instead of ten.

hook.question: How can 1 0 1 mean five?
hook.teaser: Each place is worth twice the one to its right, so the ones that are switched on add up.

children.html: In decimal, each place is worth ten times the place to its right: ones, tens, hundreds. Binary keeps the idea and uses two digits, 0 and 1, so each place is worth twice the place to its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.
Each place is worth twice the place to its right.
A single binary digit is called a bit.

children.q: In binary, what is the third place from the right worth?
children.why: The places are worth 1, 2 and then 4: each is twice the one to its right.

children.prompt: How would you explain to a friend why 101 in binary means five, in under a minute?
children.model: Binary places are worth 1, 2, 4 and so on, each twice the one to its right. 101 has a 1 in the fours place and a 1 in the ones place, and 4 + 1 = 5.

sources.title: Place value
sources.text: Each place is worth twice the place to its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16.
